newsitem.title: USA: Dlr battered at US open on EMU, Japan trade fears.
newsitem.headline: Dlr battered at US open on EMU, Japan trade fears.

text.p: The dollar opened lower as worries about Japan's trade surplus resurfaced and the mark surged in Europe amid fears France's new government might drag its heels on currency union, dealers said.

Dollar/yen slumped to a six-month low at 111.80, before rebounding somewhat in Tokyo, after selling in the wake of Friday's remarks on Japan's trade surplus by U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky spilled over on Monday.
"That started the ball rolling," said Bob Near, a vice president of corporate foreign exchange at Bank of New York.
"Then yesterday and today the (European Union) finance ministers' meeting is going on in Luxembourg, and France officially asked for a delay in consideration of the stability pact," Near continued.
Dollar/mark abruptly fell more than a pfennig to 1.7095 in European midday trade, dealers said.

The greenback took the brunt of a surge in mark/French and other mark crosses after France's Socialist-led government threw the EU into a conniption on Monday by asking its European partners for time to consult with the National Assembly over the budget stability pact for the proposed euro.

The new French Finance Minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn told his EU counterparts that Paris wanted time to reflect on the as-yet unratified plan, agreed to in Dublin in December, to contain budget deficits after the single currency debuts.
"We're not seeking to renegotiate the stability pact, but we cannot approve it today," Strauss-Kahn told a news conference.
French stocks sank after the news and mark/French jumped the 3.38 barrier. Dealers speculated the weak French franc could draw the Bank of France quietly into the market.

"Over 3.38 (mark/French), that's got to be somewhat worrisome. I would expect we would find some resistance if we got near 3.3850 or certainly 3.3875," said Frank Pusateri, a vice president at Mellon Bank in Boston.
"I wouldn't be surprised to see the Bank of France getting a little nervous and try to bring things back a little bit, if they can," he added.
The dollar opened at 1.7125/35 marks, down from 1.7245/50 at Friday's close.
Dollar/yen opened at 112.45/50, down from 114.33/43 on Friday.
Speculation Japan's trade surplus would be discussed by Group of Seven finance ministers when they gather in Denver on June 20 shoved the dollar down more than two yen in Asia.
Barshefsky sparked the refreshed concerns on Friday after she said the U.S. was worried about the potential for a rise in Japan's bilateral trade surplus with the U.S.
Dollar/yen's recovered somewhat after Japanese Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka and his deputy Tadashi Ogawa stepped in with market-soothing remarks calling for stable exchange rates.
Japan's April current account numbers are due out on Wednesday and economists expect the overall surplus to expand due to a decline in imports and sluggish domestic demand.
Elsewhere, the dollar fell to 1.4358/63 Swiss from 1.4492/02. It rose to Canadian $1.3850/55 from C$1.3835/40.
The pound rose to $1.6360/70 from $1.6315/25 and the Australian dollar inched up to $0.7609/14 from $0.7605/10 on Friday.
(( -- Alden Bentley, 212 859 1667 ))
